title: Product Photography Studios for D2C Brands: What to Look For

children.text: A practical guide for D2C teams choosing a product photography studio in India — the features that actually affect your catalogue quality, SKU-per-hour planning, and how to brief a studio shoot properly.

layout.content: Product Photography Studios for D2C Brands: What to Look For

For a D2C brand, product photography is not a creative indulgence — it is conversion infrastructure. Marketplace listings, your own storefront, performance ads, and social content all pull from the same shoot. Choosing the right product photography studio in India determines how fast you can launch SKUs and how consistent your brand looks across channels. Here's what actually matters when you evaluate studios, and how to plan a shoot that doesn't blow the budget.
Two Kinds of Product Shoots (Plan for Both)
Most D2C catalogues need two distinct looks, and the studio you pick should handle at least one of them extremely well.

items: Clean catalogue shots: white or neutral background, even lighting, marketplace-compliant — the workhorse images for Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and your product pages
Lifestyle and context shots: dressed sets, textures, models or props — the images that feed ads, Instagram, and your homepage

layout.content: Multi-set creative studios let you capture both in one booking: catalogue images on the white sweep, lifestyle content on the dressed sets. That single consolidation often cuts your total shoot cost by a third.
The Studio Checklist for Product Work

items: A proper product table or shooting sweep — not just a backdrop for people
Lighting you can shape: softboxes, diffusion, and ideally a light tent for reflective products
Macro-friendly space for jewellery, cosmetics, and small accessories
Steaming and prep area if you shoot apparel
Power, table space, and wifi for tethered shooting and on-the-spot review
Storage or trolley access for moving dozens of SKUs in and out
Set variety if you also need lifestyle content in the same slot

layout.content: How Many SKUs Can You Shoot Per Hour?

Realistic throughput planning prevents the classic mistake of booking two hours for a fifty-product catalogue. With a prepared team and a fixed lighting setup, typical rates are: simple flat-lay or on-table products at 10-15 SKUs per hour with 3-4 angles each; apparel on mannequin or model at 4-8 SKUs per hour including changes and steaming; reflective or intricate products (jewellery, glassware, electronics) at 3-6 SKUs per hour. Halve these numbers if you change lighting setups between products.
The cheapest hour in a studio is the one you prepared for at the office: label SKUs, finalize the shot list, steam garments, and charge everything the day before.
How to Brief the Shoot (Template)
Whether you bring your own photographer or use one arranged through the studio, a one-page brief keeps the day on schedule. Include:

items: SKU list in shooting order, grouped by lighting setup
Angles and variants required per SKU (front, back, detail, scale, in-use)
Reference images for the look you want — three examples beat three paragraphs
Marketplace specs: background colour, margins, minimum resolution
Priority order, so the must-haves are done before time pressure hits
File handover format and deadline for edited selects

layout.content: What D2C Product Shoots Cost in 2026

Studio space for product work in metro India typically runs ₹1,000-3,000 per hour depending on equipment and sets. A freelance product photographer adds ₹5,000-20,000 per half day depending on experience. For a 40-SKU catalogue with clean shots plus a handful of lifestyle setups, a well-planned half-day shoot lands most brands between ₹15,000 and ₹40,000 all-in — dramatically less per image than agency packages, if your team handles prep and art direction.
FAQs: Product Photography Studios
Do I need a photographer or can my team shoot the catalogue?

For marketplace-compliant catalogue shots with fixed lighting, a trained in-house person with a decent camera or recent phone can absolutely deliver — the studio's lighting does the heavy lifting. Hire a professional for lifestyle imagery, reflective products, and hero shots where composition sells the brand.
What background do Amazon and Flipkart require?

Primary marketplace images generally need a pure white background (Amazon specifies RGB 255,255,255) with the product filling most of the frame. Studios with a proper white sweep and even lighting get you there without heavy editing — confirm the studio has done marketplace work before.
How do I keep images consistent across shoots?

Document your setup: light positions, camera height, distance, and settings from the first shoot. Rebooking the same studio and reusing that setup sheet keeps a growing catalogue visually uniform — one of the strongest arguments for building a relationship with one or two studios rather than hopping.
Can I shoot video for ads in the same booking?

Yes, and you should — short product videos and reels-format clips convert strongly in performance ads. Add 30-60 minutes to the slot, keep the lighting setup, and capture rotation shots, hands-on-product B-roll, and unboxing sequences while everything is staged.

Final Takeaways

Great product photography is a planning problem before it's a creative one. Pick a studio with real product infrastructure, plan SKU throughput honestly, and consolidate catalogue plus lifestyle work into single bookings.

items: Choose studios with a product table, shapeable lighting, and prep space
Plan 10-15 simple SKUs per hour; far fewer for apparel and reflective items
Brief in writing with references and a priority order
Capture ad video in the same slot while the set is staged
